articles.title: Sandigan suspends Martin for 90 days
articles.summary: As his trial for plunder continues, former House speaker Martin Romualdez has been ordered suspended for 90 days by the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

blocks.text: November 11, 2026 | 12:00am
Martin Romualdez on October 24, 2025
The STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — As his trial for plunder continues, former House speaker Martin Romualdez has been ordered suspended for 90 days by the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

“The court issued a resolution ordering the suspension pendente lite of former speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez for a period of 90 days from the receipt of resolution,” Third Division clerk of court Dennis Pulma said yesterday.
Romualdez was ordered to “cease and desist” from the functions of his office or any other office.
The P7.4-billion plunder case against the suspended Leyte representative stemmed from his having allegedly received kickback from flood control projects.

The Sandiganbayan also directed the Romualdez camp to furnish a copy of the resolution to the speaker of the House of Representatives through the Office of the Secretary General. Both offices are requested to inform the court of any action taken within five days from the receipt of the resolution.
Prosecutors from the Office of the Ombudsman have accused Romualdez of being the central figure in an alleged scheme involving the diversion of public funds meant for flood control projects.
The other accused in the plunder case are fugitive former Ako Bicol party-list representative Zaldy Co, former Romualdez personal assistant Joselyn Serenio and businessman Felicito Guevarra.

During the bail hearing on Romualdez’s plunder case, Navotas Rep. Tobias Tiangco testified that he saw red flags on the insertions made by his colleagues in House of Representatives in the 2025 budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways based on files forwarded to him by the late DPWH undersecretary Maria Catalina Cabral.
He said he found P26 billion worth of projects that listed Romualdez as the proponent even if most of them were not in the former House leader’s legislative district.

Among the districts that reportedly received projects from Romualdez were Davao City and Davao del Norte, although he acknowledged that his conclusions were based partly on his own interpretation and on information obtained from other individuals.
Under questioning, Tiangco conceded that he had no personal knowledge of any cash delivery or whether such deliveries had indeed happened.
He admitted that some of the “red flags” he found were merely his own interpretation of the files from Cabral, wherein some of the projects’ locations and sums were “doubtful.”
He also pointed out that being listed as a proponent does not automatically mean that the same person receives money through commissions.

Tiangco, who served as one of the vice chairs of the appropriations committee under Co, also admitted that he participated in the budget process, including defending the proposed appropriations of agencies assigned to him, such as the Office of the President and the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development.
He also acknowledged voting in favor of the proposed 2025 national budget during plenary deliberations.

Tiangco likewise confirmed that Romualdez did not participate in the appropriations committee hearings or during plenary deliberations on the budget, and was not a member of the House small committee or the bicameral conference committee.

While alleging that Co implemented Romualdez’s instructions during the bicameral deliberations, Tiangco acknowledged that he was not a member of the bicameral panel and had no personal knowledge of its proceedings during the 19th Congress.
Tiangco also testified that President Marcos reprimanded Romualdez in 2024 for allegedly taking funds meant for government projects.

articles.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
articles.summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of…

image.caption: The apparent cyberattack forced hundreds of supermarkets to throw out spoiled produce after the refrigeration and freezer units went into a high-temperature defrost cycleImage: Elsa Rancel/Ouest-France/PHOTOPQR/MAXPPP/IMAGO

blocks.text: Iran on Tuesday dismissed French accusations that its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was behind a cyberattack on hundreds of supermarkets last month, as Paris summoned Tehran's ambassador to discuss the incident.

"Iran's Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government's baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France," the ministry said, adding that it "strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of leveling accusations against the Islamic Republic."
The alleged attack, which began overnight on October 11-12, raised the temperatures in supermarket refrigerators and freezer units, spoiling produce and even causing fires in isolated instances.

A series of similar incidents have since followed in Europe and beyond, even including a failed attack on cooling units at French blood banks this month, though it is not yet clear if these subsequent events are connected.
France summons ambassador, says it rules 'nothing' out in response

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday that his government would "rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks."
Barrot was speaking amid a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that included discussions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the conflict with Iran.

Barrot even said that despite a change in tone from the Trump administration since the midterm election defeat in the US, the risk of a renewed escalation with Iran could not be ruled out, "otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues with our American counterpart."

blocks.caption: Barrot hosted G7 foreign ministers, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in Paris this weekImage: Brendan Smialowski/REUTERS

blocks.text: France summoned the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday and said it would be seeking European-level sanctions in response.
The EU said it would seek to provide a "swift and united response" pending discussion with member states.

"As the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behavior in the cyberspace, and we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have, also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions," spokesman Anouar El Anouni said.
Barrot said that the goal of any response would be "to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again."
Iran accuses French of 'projecting' its own failures

Tehran appeared to threaten retaliatory measures of its own if sanctions materialized, saying it would "not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities."
It accused France of "merely projecting its own governance failures" with its allegations.
"A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations," it said.

blocks.caption: Around 700 supermarkets, of a total of roughly 10,000 across France, were affected by the alleged cyberattackImage: Stephane Mahe/REUTERS

blocks.text: What did Paris prosecutors say about suspected Iranian involvement?

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said on Monday that she had opened an investigation into leading members of Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit that is part of Iran's multi-force specialist military, the IRGC, that answers directly to its religious leadership.
She said her office had requested arrest warrants against two Shahid Kaveh officials and was investigating others.
She described the entity as "an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Electronic and Cyber Center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps."

French cyber intelligence agencies said the unit conducted "large-scale campaigns targeting industrial equipment for the purpose of sabotage." It said it primarily targeted Israel and the US, but also France and other European countries.

Beccuau said that the attack targeted roughly 700 of France's roughly 10,000 supermarkets. It used web interfaces to "initiate abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles," and also to disable automated alerts from sensors designed to go off when temperatures exceeded certain levels.
Sweden's Civil Defense Minister Carl-Oskar Bohlin warned that more cyberattacks could be expected in the coming months, as AI tools make it easier to detect and exploit vulnerabilities.

He said that it was not yet possible to say if hacks targeted Swedish supermarkets last week were connected, not least because the type of sabotage would have "been easy to copy" after seeing the initial reports in October.

articles.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
articles.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they…

image.caption: European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence [Pictured: Clearing of land by setting grass on fire during a German research expedition to Tendaguru in German East Africa, 1909-1913]Image: Archiv/Museum für Naturkunde

blocks.text: Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: at first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring "like the English, we shall rule this empire with handful of men."

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire, and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared, remains the subject of intense debate. This is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

blocks.caption: 'Murder for the very purpose of murder': The industrialized mass murder carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau had no direct precedent in colonial historyImage: Taiftin/Depositphotos/IMAGO

blocks.text: "I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposed to be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case."

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a new exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.
From colonial brutality to Nazi rule

The exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust. Yet it also points to connections: whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

blocks.caption: The extreme brutality of Fascist Italy's invasion of Ethiopia, including the use of chemical weapons, caused uproar around the world [Pictured: The bombing of the Ethiopian village of Dessye by Italian planes on December 9, 1935]Image: Topfoto/United Archives International/IMAGO

blocks.text: In the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing new or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people."

European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

blocks.caption: One of the most notorious symbols of King Leopold II's rule was the amputation of hands, inflicted on men, women and children who failed to meet rubber production quotas [Pictured: A Congolese child with an amputated hand, 1900]Image: United Archives/World History Archive/IMAGO

blocks.text: The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations, and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met. Forced labor was central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.
Racism, antisemitism and extermination

While racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski says the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

"In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued."

blocks.caption: From 1904 to 1908, German colonial rule in present-day Namibia culminated in the genocide of the Herero and Nama, in which tens of thousands died [Pictured:  Concentration camp for Herero and Nama in German South West Africa, 1905]Image: Sam-Cohen-Bibliothek/Scientific Society Swakopmund

blocks.text: On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor, and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

One area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic: even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.
The politics of historical comparison

The issue of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

blocks.caption: After being deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1943, French artist David Olère depicted scenes he witnessed. Here, deportees arrive at a crematorium shortly before their murder [Pictured: David Olère, 'Vers la mort' ('On the Way to Death'), Paris, 1945]Image: Mémorial de la Shoah/Coll. David Olère

blocks.text: The mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator said what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.
Rethinking Germany's culture of remembrance

Martinican intellectual Aimé Césaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

Germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance. However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human-beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi said. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity."
"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
articles.summary:
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent

Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet…
articles.byline: Associated Press at the Rafah crossing

blocks.text: Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.

The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October.

A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
Israeli forces have continued to advance, expanding their control from 53% of the territory to at least 60%, an independent commission of UN experts said last month.

blocks.caption: Lewis Hamilton (in black) listens to an Egyptian Red Crescent official during a visit to a logistics centre in Al-Arish. Photograph: Mohammed Arafat/AP

blocks.text: Airstrikes also continue, and Israeli fire along the advancing front has killed at least 196 Palestinians, including 18 women, 32 boys and 11 girls, the commission said.
Hamilton toured Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with Gaza before visiting logistics warehouses operated by the Egyptian Red Crescent, which facilitates the entry of aid to Gaza.
At the crossing, Hamilton greeted aid workers with “Assalamu alaikum” a widely used Arabic greeting meaning “peace be upon you.” He shook hands and briefly spoke to workers and officials.
Khaled Megawer, the governor of North Sinai, where Rafah is located, said the visit was intended to help Hamilton learn about Egypt’s efforts to send aid to Gaza.
The visit comes after Hamilton made his 400th race start on Sunday at the São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos.
The first black F1 driver, he made his debut with McLaren in 2007. He is only the second F1 driver to start 400 races after his former teammate Fernando Alonso, who achieved the milestone in 2024.

articles.title: Poland: Krakow shooting suspect 'fascinated' by Norwegian mass murder Anders Breivik, says justice minister
articles.summary: The 24-year old suspect was found to have read a significant amount of material about Breivik and other far-right figures. Speculation over his motives have prompted a bitter political feud in Warsaw.

image.caption: The suspect, now deceased, is suspected of radicalization and severe psychiatric issuesImage: Jakub Porzycki/REUTERS

blocks.text: Polish Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek issued an update on Tuesday concerning the case of a mass shooting in Krakow over the weekend.
Accused gunman Michal Oksinski was deeply interested in international far-right movements, Zurek said.
"Authorities have accessed the terrorist's computer. It is clear that he visited websites concerning Anders Breivik," the Norwegian neo-Nazi who killed 77 people in July 2011, the minister added.
Zurek said a search of Oksinski's home turned up a Gadsen flag, a banner dating back to the US Civil War that is now associated with American white nationalists.
Police also gathered evidence that he had recently bought 10 magazines for a semi-automatic rifle and 500 bullets.
"It is clear that this individual was preparing to take action," the justice minister said.
Krakow shooting suspect 'fascinated by far right'
What happened in the attack?
On Friday night, 24-year-old Oksinski is thought to have shot and killed his mother, father, sister and two family cats in the city of Ostrowiec.

The following day at around 3:00 p.m. local time, Oksinski is suspected of opening fire in Krakow's Main Market Square. Six people were killed — four Poles, one Austrian, and one UK national. Another 15 people were wounded.
After the attack in Krakow, authorities discovered the bodies of his family members in Ostrowiec.
Poland then observed two days of national mourning. Oksinski died of wounds sustained during his arrest at a local hospital on Monday.
Initial investigations have uncovered "very solid" evidence pointing to far-right radicalization and psychiatric issues as motives for the attacks, Zurek said.
However, Zurek and the centrist government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk has been accused by members of right-wing populist PiS party of lying about Oksinski's motives.

articles.title: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.summary: The group, formed by Trump, issues rare criticism of Israel, while also blaming Hamas for the suffering of civilians in Gaza.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has called on Israel to immediately allow all necessary humanitarian supplies into Gaza after rain flooded tens of thousands of tents.
The US-backed body, established to oversee the implementation of Trump's Gaza peace plan, acknowledged the steps now being considered by Israel, but said "the response remains insufficient".

Israel's military agency in charge of co-ordinating aid into Gaza said it had allowed in tens of thousands of tents and trucks with winter supplies, but added reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".
On Sunday, three children and a woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in the central Strip.
Most people in Gaza have been displaced because of Israel's military actions. Around 65% of the population, about 1.4 million people, now live in tents or makeshift shelters, the UN says.

Standing soaked in Gaza City, Mohammed Jneid told the AFP news agency that heavy rains hit from one side and sewage overflowed on them from the other, with the ground and tents no longer able to hold.
"We have nothing left, no bedding, no food, nothing," he said.
Sitting inside her tent, Islam Al Mobayed told AFP there were seven children there, five of them young.
"This is not life," she said. "We are exhausted, we are tired of this entire life."
In rare criticism of Israel, the Board of Peace said it had been urging the Israeli government to authorise the entry of essential goods for temporary shelter and water and sanitation infrastructure.

The Board added that delays in approving the entry of supplies "exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge" and delayed the start of decommissioning weapons and transferring Hamas authority to a transitional government.
It also said Hamas's failure to disarm and transfer power had compounded the difficulties facing Gaza's civilians.

The UN's humanitarian agency OCHA said more than 150,000 tents were outside Gaza ready to go in, but aid efforts were constrained "by Israeli restrictions on the entry of supplies and equipment and funding shortfalls".
UN humanitarian coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said on Monday that stocks of essential shelter and winter items inside Gaza had been exhausted.
"Israeli authorities must immediately lift all restrictions on entry of the supplies," he said, adding "we have run out of time".
Israel's foreign ministry spokeswoman Michal Maayan on Monday said Israel had in recent months put in place a winter plan in coordination with the Board of Peace and international charities.

That plan has brought in more than 91,000 tents and 8,200-plus trucks with tarpaulins, blankets, winter clothing, and other equipment, according to Cogat, the Israeli military body responsible for aid.
Cogat said it would not allow in equipment that could be used for military purposes.
Maayon accused Hamas of hoarding aid, saying: "Hamas is responsible for the delays in making more progress in the Strip, and winter-related hardships are a consequence of Hamas's action and policy."

In response to the Board of Peace, Hamas said in a statement published on Palestinian media that its comment "presents a distorted account of the causes of the disaster". The group denied it was responsible for ceasefire delays, pointing to a statement in August , externalfrom Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators that accused Israel of violations.
Hamas said Israeli restrictions prevent the entry of materials necessary for shelter and recovery - and added the Board as the ceasefire implementor should look at its own "serious shortcoming".

Under the deal to end the two-year-long war in October 2025, Hamas agreed to give up governance and its weapons in exchange for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal from the 60% of Gaza it still occupied. Israel, however, has insisted Hamas must fully disarm before withdrawal.
The dispute has left the next stages of the peace plan stalled, with both sides blaming each other.
The war in Gaza began after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 when around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.

The Israeli military campaign in response has killed 74,645 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN considers reliable. More than 1,600 people have been killed since the ceasefire in October last year.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza since then.

articles.title: Sara Duterte's P64,000 Davao payout not reflected in 2024 ITR, prosecution says
articles.summary: The P64,000 payout that Vice President Sara Duterte received from the Davao City government in 2023 for her services as city mayor was not reflected in her income tax return (ITR) for the following…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 11:14pm

The P64,000 payout that Vice President Sara Duterte received from the Davao City government in 2023 for her services as city mayor was not reflected in her income tax return (ITR) for the following year, the House prosecution panel said Tuesday.

Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia made the claim, citing Duterte’s 2024 ITR, which did not indicate any compensation received from either the Davao City government or the Office of the Vice President (OVP).

Divinagracia then asked defense witness and Davao City Accountant Vingelin Bajan to confirm that Duterte’s 2024 ITR did not include compensation from either office. However, Bajan declined to give an answer.
“I cannot answer, Attorney,” Bajan said.

Bajan submitted photocopies of payroll summaries and disbursement vouchers, among other documents, showing that the P64,194.72 salary differential paid to Duterte covered the periods January to December 2020 and January to December 2021.
Bajan, however, said the payout was made only in January 2023 because the supporting documents were completed only at that time.
She also said she no longer had the original copies because these had already been submitted to the Commission on Audit (COA).
Divinagracia then asked Bajan if she had documentary proof that the COA had received the payroll summaries.
Bajan replied that transmitting such documents to the COA was the practice.

Divinagracia pointed out that this was not what she had asked and pressed Bajan to confirm: “In short, you do not have proof that these original documents are already in the possession of COA. Is that correct?”
Bajan replied, “Yes, Ma'am. Hindi ko po nadala po.”
(I was not able to bring them.)

Meanwhile, Senator Raffy Tulfo and Senate impeachment court Presiding Officer Francis Escudero questioned the handwritten corrections on some of the disbursement vouchers submitted by Bajan. The documents originally indicated the period January to December 2022, but this was later changed to January to December 2020 and January to December 2021.

Asked why the corrections were countersigned by hand, Bajan said the changes were made after supporting documents showed that the payouts to Duterte, now the Vice President, covered the periods January to December 2020 and January to December 2021.
“It was corrected on December 30, 2022,” Bajan said.
Tulfo then asked whether the correction was made belatedly, noting that the Constitution prohibits the Vice President from receiving double compensation.
Bajan attributed the delay to the lengthy process of preparing the disbursement vouchers. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
articles.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

image.caption: Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off on Saturday due to pain in his right footImage: Attila Ziga/Eibner-Pressefoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: It's no secret that getting playing time is important to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

Unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.
What could Neuer's injury change?

But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.
An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.
"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.
"I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can."

A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

blocks.caption: Jonas Urbig replaced Manuel Neuer on Saturday and is expected to take over full time in the futureImage: Jürgen Kessler/Kessler-Sportfotografie/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The goalkeeper of the future

Although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

The match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.
One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.
At some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment."

For now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.
This article was adapted from German.

The skate takes place at 11:30 a.m., so the livestream is scheduled to begin around 12:15 p.m., though it's not clear yet when Hellebuyck will start speaking.

New Jersey general manager Sunny Mehta announced Sunday, after Hellebuyck and his team posted a 4-0 shutout win over Toronto, that the star goaltender would not play in his first return to the city where he spent 11 NHL seasons.
"Playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability," Mehta's statement said, despite Hellebuyck being undefeated so far in five games with the Devils.
Goaltender Connor Hellebuyck was traded to the New Jersey Devils late last month after 11 seasons with the Winnipeg Jets. (Seth Wenig/The Associated Press)
In his post-game interview on Sunday, Hellebuyck said he wanted to face his former team but understands the Devils' decision and "it's out of my hands."
At Hellebuyck's request, the team has co-ordinated a media availability after the morning skate at Canada Life Centre, Mehta's statement said.
Backup goalies typically skate in the pre-game warmup, which might be the only chance for Jets fans to see him.
There’s no room for backup goalies on the visiting team’s bench in Canada Life Centre, so Hellebuyck won’t be exposed to greetings from the crowd during the game.
Hellebuyck's trade out of Winnipeg followed a prolonged and strained end to his career as a Jet and has left many fans bitter.

He made his trade request at the end of last season, just two years after committing to a seven-year contract extension and declaring, "I’m ready to be a Jet for life and bring a Cup to this city, because I truly believe we can get it done here."

items: Connor Hellebuyck posts open letter 'to the great Jets fans'

blocks.text: When the requested trade hadn't been made before training camp started in fall, Hellebuyck failed to show up, so the Jets suspended him.
He was traded the day that suspension was set to end.
Following the trade on Oct. 23, fans circled Nov. 10 on their calendars. It's the only visit by the Devils this season, though the teams meet up again Nov. 28 when the Jets play in New Jersey.
Tickets for Tuesday's game sold out quickly and prices tripled in some cases.
Jets fans and head coach Scott Arniel expressed disappointment that Hellebuyck is not suiting up for the game.

articles.title: UK and Argentina clash over Falklands oil project as Hamburg tribunal starts
articles.summary:
Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin threatens to deepen sovereignty dispute

Argentina has told an international tribunal that Britain’s approval of oil drilling off the Falkland…

blocks.text: Argentina has told an international tribunal that Britain’s approval of oil drilling off the Falkland Islands has dramatically deepened a sovereignty dispute that led to war four decades ago.
At the start of an historic legal clash at the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (Itlos), an Argentinian legal team argued that the oil project must be suspended.

Javier Oyarzábal, chief legal adviser to Argentina’s ministry of foreign affairs, said that the 3,400 inhabitants of the Falkland Islands, whose status as a British overseas territory is disputed by Buenos Aires, had no right to the resources around the south Atlantic archipelago.

Oyarzábal said: “[Argentina] respects the interests of the inhabitants of the islands and their way of life as enshrined in the Argentine constitution … What these British citizens do not have is a right to decide to which state the islands belong …
“These resources belong to the Argentine people. Some 46 million of them including the 1,247 inhabitants born on the islands whose interests will be duly taken into account.”

Oyarzábal said Argentina was ready to negotiate “all aspects of the question” of the Falkland Islands, which are known as the Malvinas in Argentina, “including the present aggravation of the dispute caused by the UK”.
He accused the UK of refusing to enter talks over the islands while pushing forward on the exploitation of its natural resources in a way that would entrench the status quo.
Oyarzábal claimed that the oil money from the drilling would “finance the very military base and presence that sustains the UK’s de facto control of the territory”.

Addressing the panel’s chair, Judge Maurice Kamga, from Cameroon, he added: “Mr President, the UK cannot have it both ways. It cannot invoke the sovereignty dispute to escape jurisdiction [of Itlos] while exploiting the natural resources of the disputed area as if a dispute had already been resolved in its favour.”
The Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin, led by the Israeli-firm Navitas and its British partner, Rockhopper, has the potential to triple the islands’ GDP per capita.

It has been condemned as unlawful by Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, and his government has applied for arbitration by Itlos over the future of the project, claiming Britain’s approval of is in breach of a 1976 UN resolution calling on both parties to desist from unilateral action on the islands until the sovereignty dispute is settled.

Argentina is requesting urgent provisional measures, including a commitment from the UK to “stop the drilling” which, Oyarzábal said would do no more than “preserve the present situation” and allow for constructive talks over sovereignty to begin.

At the start of the two-day hearing, the tribunal’s panel was told that a decision by the UK government to allow drilling to start in March next year was the “unilateral conduct” of a “colonial power”.

It was further claimed by Argentina that the Sea Lion oil project risked an environmental disaster on Argentina’s doorstep and that it would make the sovereignty dispute over the islands “more difficult or impossible” to resolve peacefully.

He added: “In the event of a blowout or spill, it is Argentina that would bear its consequences and be called upon to respond, not a state that is 12,700km away. More over the project lies within the search and rescue region for which Argentina is responsible”.

The long-standing dispute between Argentina and the UK over the sovereignty of the Falklands led to war in 1982 at the cost of the lives of 649 Argentine military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland Islanders.
The hearing is the first time that substantive matters relating to the Falklands have been litigated at an international tribunal.

The oil project is seen on the islands as offering the opportunity to secure their economic future, and build a sovereign wealth fund, at a time when fisheries catches on which they depend are declining.
In a show of solidarity, Princess Anne arrived in Port Stanley on Monday. Ellie Reeves, the UK’s attorney general, attended the Itlos hearing on Tuesday.

She claimed that Argentina was seeking to litigate the issue of sovereignty through Itlos, an independent judicial body established by the 1982 United Nations convention on the law of the sea to oversee maritime disputes.
She said: “We don’t think this is the forum to effectively determine sovereignty issues.”

Asked whether the UK would abide by any ruling, Reeves said: “We don’t know what’s going to happen in terms of the outcome but we don’t consider they have jurisdiction on sovereignty issues. We respect the court and the institutions … but I don’t want to get ahead of what the tribunal may or may not say.” The hearing continues.

articles.title: Prosecution seeks sanctions vs. VP Sara, spokesperson over alleged sub judice violations
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel has asked the Senate impeachment court to sanction Vice President Sara Duterte and her spokesperson, Atty. Paolo Panelo, over statements that allegedly violated the sub…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 10:41pm

The House prosecution panel has asked the Senate impeachment court to sanction Vice President Sara Duterte and her spokesperson, Atty. Paolo Panelo, over statements that allegedly violated the sub judice rule, including remarks that supposedly questioned the integrity of the court.

Private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. made the call on Tuesday after lead defense counsel Sheila Sison urged the court to take action over Tolosa’s statements, which she claimed delved into the merits of the impeachment case against the Vice President in violation of the sub judice rule.
Senate impeachment court Presiding Officer Francis Escudero said the court had been looking into statements made by both parties over the weekend that may have violated the sub judice rule.

“We've heard that from the Vice President time and again, as well as her spokesperson attacking their integrity, attacking their motives, saying the impeachment proceedings have been marred by bending the law, saying that senators are manipulating the proceedings, and that the budget is being used to control the senators. These [statements] touched not just the merits of the case but also attack the integrity of the court,” Tolosa said in a press conference.

“We've always been asking for a fair shake. One court, one rule—let's apply them evenly. I am quite sure no one from the prosecution said anything that could be remotely considered to have attacked the integrity of the court and not even one senator-judge,” he added.
Tolosa said the statements from the Vice President's camp were intended to condition the minds of her supporters into believing that the proceedings were not legitimate.

“That’s why we will be asking the court to take action not just on the statements of the Vice President but also on the statements given by her spokesperson that have repeatedly violated the sub judice rule as well and which are even contemptuous in nature,” he added.
Tolosa also said he was prepared to respond to Sison's allegations.

“We look forward to receiving this motion that they may be filing, and we will respond to it accordingly. We've always respected the sub judice rule and the court's authority and integrity, as well as the integrity of the proceedings,” Tolosa said. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos: Gov't saved P1.4 billion in MacBook deal for DepEd teachers, staff
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the government was able to save P1.4 billion in its deal with Apple Inc., where it secured MacBook Neo laptops well below the unit"s suggested retail price in the…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the government was able to save P1.4 billion in its deal with Apple Inc., where it secured MacBook Neo laptops well below the unit’s suggested retail price in the Philippines.

“Mas mura ang bawat laptop kumpara sa karaniwang presyo nito sa merkado. Kasama din dito ang delivery, limang taon warranty, software at training,” Marcos said in a “24 Oras” report by Ivan Mayrina on Tuesday.
(Each laptop is cheaper compared to its regular market price. This also includes delivery, a five-year warranty, software, and training.)
“Dahil dito, nakatipid ang ating pamahalaan ng P1.4 billion. Ang anumang natipid ay mailalaan sa ibang pangangailangan natin sa edukasyon,” he added.
(Because of this, our government saved P1.4 billion. Whatever is saved can be allocated to our other educational needs.)
The Department of Education (DepEd) secured more than 172,000 MacBook Neo laptops under the deal. Each unit was reportedly procured at P43,000, which is P6,900 lower than its current market price.
Apple described this landmark procurement as its "biggest education deal ever" for its MacBook line.
Amid concerns of overpricing and overspending, Education Secretary Sonny Angara assured that the deal underwent competitive bidding.

“Dito may proseso hong pinagdaraanan and that's called the competitive bidding under the Procurement Law. Definitely ang importante yung specs na maganda at ‘yung pabor talaga sa ating mga educators,” Angara said.
(Here, there is a process we undergo, and that's called competitive bidding under the Procurement Law. Definitely, what's important are good specs that truly favor our educators.)
Laptop distribution
In Dagupan City, more than 200 teachers have already been given some of the new MacBook Neo laptops.
Among them is Alysa Curameng, a teacher from West Central Elementary School, who envisions the new unit making their workload and lessons significantly easier.

“Lalo pong mapapadali ang ating trabaho at pagtuturo. Sa part po kasi ng laptop, kapag once na napuno na ‘yon… talagang, as in, nahihirapan din po ang mga teacher lalo na laging nalo-loading… as in talagang puno na,” Curameng said.

(It will truly make our work and teaching easier. As for the previous laptops, once they get full... it really becomes difficult for teachers, especially since they keep lagging when it’s completely full.)
Under DepEd’s Computerization Program, a total of 231,000 laptops will be distributed across the country. The rollout runs from November 2026 until March 2027.
Of the laptops to be distributed, more than 169,000 are MacBook Neos, while over 62,000 are Windows-based.
In Mayrina’s report, the government also distributed 3,646 MacBook Neo units to DepEd administrative officers.
With over 800,000 public school teachers nationwide, the department admitted it cannot yet provide a 1:1 laptop ratio.
However, under agency guidelines, priority in receiving new units is given to teachers who have not yet received any government-issued laptop.
Angara emphasized that while the gadgets are issued to teachers, they remain government property.
“Government property po ‘yan. ‘Pag binenta ho nila ‘yan, e di babayaran nila ‘yan. The IT officer, each school has an IT officer, so siya ‘yung parang custodian,” Angara noted.
(That is government property. If they sell that, they will pay for it. There is an IT officer in every school who acts as the custodian.) – Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it…

image.caption: The logo of data center company Megaspeed International at its office in the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore on November 10, 2026Image: Taryn Ng/AFP

blocks.text: As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for.

Alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing company. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

According to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the company advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

This type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies.

The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.
Megaspeed's mega rise
Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

blocks.caption: Megaspeed managed data centers for Chinese tech giant AlibabaImage: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.
At the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.
On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the company's website as of November 2026.

"There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it said. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct."

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the New York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.
A brief history

Megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.
Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the company's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.
The relationship with Nvidia
The Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.
Nvidia investigates CEO after reports of affair with Chinese spy

The newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.
Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

In December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the company was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.
China and the battle for chips
Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.
Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.
Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.
However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.
In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell company with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

blocks.caption: Nvidia's chips are seen as the gold standard for AI applicationsImage: Kobe Li/ZUMAPRESS/picture alliance

blocks.text: In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.
While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.
In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

blocks.text: Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.

One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor hotel in Paris.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.

"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."

The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."

articles.title: How Sara Duterte witness is linked to auditor of Mans Carpio’s firms
articles.summary: 'So, para sa akin...parang may koneksiyon sa inyo itong external auditing firm,' Senator Sherwin Gatchalian tells Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan

blocks.text: WITNESS. Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan takes the witness stand on Day 41 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on November 10, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit
'So, para sa akin...parang may koneksiyon sa inyo itong external auditing firm,' Senator Sherwin Gatchalian tells Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan

items: Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team called accountant Vingelin Bajan as a witness, who struggled to recall details related to her previous work with the Elises and Ciudadano accounting firm.

During cross-examination, Bajan was questioned about her ties to the firm and its connections to companies associated with Duterte's husband, but she repeatedly stated she could not remember key information.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team brought Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan as their second witness for her trial. She testified on Tuesday, November 10, a day after Davao City assessor Jaime Adalin.

But coming from Davao City is not the only common denominator between the two officials. They were also both flagged by the impeachment court for failing to recall things connected — either directly or indirectly — to their job.

Both the senator-judges and the prosecution grilled Bajan over her ties to the Elises and Ciudadano accounting firm (formerly known as Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano and Co.) Prosecutor Mae Divinagracia showed documents supposedly showing Bajan’s involvement with the firm.
At one point, Divinagracia showed a copy of amended articles of general partnership that supposedly removed the accountant’s name from the firm in 2015, but Bajan said she could not recall anything.
“Hindi ko na maalala (I could no longer remember),” said the accountant. “Hindi ko po ma-remember, your honor (I could not remember). Sorry.”
Bajan later confirmed that she’s no longer part of the firm but still insisted that she no longer remembers the document being presented to her.

“Miss Evan, parte kayo ng accounting firm, hindi ‘nyo maalala kung kailan kayo umalis o kung finile po ‘yan? Nasa harap ‘nyo na po ‘yong dokumento?” presiding officer Chiz Escudero asked. (Miss Evan, you are part of the accounting firm, you cannot remember when you left or if that document was filed? Even if the document is already in front of you?)
Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo then interjected and said he fears for Bajan because of her failure to answer the questions directed at her.

“Kung ngayon pa nga lang, sa signature pa nga lang, hindi mo na kayang sagutin, ‘yon pa kayang mahihirap na katanungan later on? Baka ma-contempt ka,” warned Tulfo. (If we’re only talking about signatures and you cannot answer already, what more with the harder questions later on? You might be held in contempt.)
“Sign ko po ito (This is my signature), your honor,” said Bajan later on.
After establishing Bajan’s link to the firm, the prosecution proceeded to the point of its cross-examination — to cast doubt on the witness’ credibility.

Divinagracia pressed Bajan to confirm whether the auditing firm she previously worked for was the same firm that served as external auditor of the companies connected to Mans Carpio, the Vice President’s husband.
As it appeared, the firm had a working relationship with Gencorp Industries and Metro City Chow Foods, among others.
Again, the witness said she did not know.

blocks.caption: How Sara Duterte witness is linked to auditor of Mans Carpio’s firms

blocks.text: “‘Yong external auditor po ng Gencorp is Elises, Ciudadano, from 2019 onwards. And ‘yong Metro City Chow, from 2020 onwards, sila rin po ang external auditor. Pero napansin ko rin po dito po sa external auditor ni Attorney Manases at ni Vice President Sara ay Elises, Ciudadano rin,” said Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.
“So, para sa akin…parang nagkakaroon ng koneksiyon ‘yong partnership sa Elises, Ciudadano…. Parang may koneksiyon sa inyo itong external auditing firm,” he added.

(Gencorp’s external auditor from 2019 onwards is Elises, Ciudadano. And from 2020 onwards, it is also Metro City Chow’s external auditor. But I also noticed that Elises, Ciudadano is also the external auditor of Attorney Mans and Vice President Sara. So, for me, there’s a connection in the partnership with Elises, Ciudadano. It seems the external auditing firm has a connection to you.)
“Hindi ko po alam ‘yon (I don’t know that), your honor,” said Bajan. – Rappler.com

articles.title: More than 300 domestic flights could be affected by ASEAN Summit, says DOTr
articles.summary: More than 300 domestic flights could be affected amid the arrival of world leaders in the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 10:12pm
More than 300 domestic flights could be affected amid the arrival of world leaders in the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said Tuesday.
In a “24 Oras” report by Bernadette Reyes, the department advised passengers to check their airlines' websites or contact them directly for the status of their flights.
Passengers with canceled flights are entitled to a free rebooking, a full refund, or the option to store the amount in a travel fund for future use, according to DOTr.
For individuals with unaffected flights, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon encouraged them to head to the airport earlier than usual to avoid delays.

“Plan your trip properly. Kung ang international [flight] ninyo dati two hours before, gawin ninyo nang tatlong oras kasi syempre may mga darating nang mga heads of state, medyo may disruption ng kaunti,” Dizon said.
(Plan your trip properly. If you usually arrive two hours before your international flight, make it three hours this time because with heads of state arriving, there will be minor disruptions.)
The ASEAN Summit is scheduled for November 16 to 18, 2026. However, passengers are already experiencing heavy congestion on roads near the airport.
“Grabe ang traffic talaga. Umalis kami 6:30 [a.m.] nakarating kami dito 9:30 [a.m.] galing sa North Caloocan,” Weng Villodes shared, who dropped off her child at the airport.
(The traffic is really terrible. We left North Caloocan at 6:30 a.m. and only arrived here at 9:30 a.m.)

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) has issued traffic and road advisories for the upcoming Summit, including security exclusion zones, roads subject to stop-and-go schemes, and alternate routes for trucks.
A week away from the Summit, access to the Cultural Center of the Philippines complex has already been restricted, with only authorized personnel and vehicles allowed to enter the vicinity.

In Reyes’ report, some motorists are still adjusting to the new traffic advisories due to the lack of adequate road signage, though MMDA enforcers and police officers are on site to guide traffic flow.
Clearing operations
In preparation for the ASEAN Summit, the government has also implemented clearing operations, which Malacañang described as part of its security measures.

“Malaking bagay po na maipakita natin na tayo ay isang bansa na makapagbigay ng sapat na seguridad sa mga liderato na pupunta sa ating bansa. At dapat natin ipakita… ‘yung hospitality na nakapaloob sa Pilipino,” Palace Press Officer Under Secretary Claire Castro said.
(It is crucial that we demonstrate our capability to provide adequate security for the leaders visiting our country. We must also show... the hospitality inherent in Filipinos.)
Castro appealed to progressive groups to defer their rallies until after the summit.
“Kung anuman ‘yung maaapektuhan, kung may kinakailangan na transportasyon na maapektuhan ng gagawing pagra-rally ito ay tutugunan ng gobyerno," she added.
(Whatever may be affected, if there is any transportation affected by the planned rallies, the government is ready to address it.) –Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Victorian Labor’s ‘unforgivable’ preferences decision risks Liberal-One Nation government, Greens warn
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Ellen Sandell says Labor’s decision not to back progressives in key inner-seat could hand power to right-wing coalition in close election

  • Get our

blocks.text: The Victorian Greens say Labor’s “frankly unforgivable” decision not to preference the minor party in a key inner-city seat could hand the upcoming election to a Liberal-One Nation coalition.

The party’s leader, Ellen Sandell, lambasted Labor’s decision on Tuesday to run an open ticket in Prahran, an inner Melbourne seat currently held by the Liberals’ Rachel Westaway on a tiny 1.3% margin.

It means Labor’s how-to-vote material will encourage voters to place their candidate, Meghan Hopper, first on the ballot but will not direct them how to allocate their remaining preferences. Instead, the remaining boxes on its how-to-vote material will probably remain blank.
Labor preferences are key to the Greens cinching back the seat, which they lost in a 2025 byelection.

The Greens received a 13.4% swing at the poll, with the result influenced by several factors, including Labor’s decision not to field a candidate, low voter turnout, a well-resourced campaign urging voters to put them last and unfavourable preference flows from other candidates. This included the former Labor MP Tony Lupton, who contested the byelection as an independent.

Sandell told Guardian Australia Labor was “showing its true colours” by running an open ticket, as it could inadvertently help the Liberals and One Nation not only secure the seat but also government.
“After months of scaremongering about a Liberal-One Nation government, Labor is now using its preferences to help elect one,” she said.
“This could be one of the most consequential elections in the state’s history. The result may come down to a single seat, and a divisive party like One Nation could hold the balance of power.
“It is frankly unforgivable that Labor would do a dodgy back-room deal to help elect a Liberal-One Nation government – and it’s something that Victorian voters will not easily forget.”
Sandell said Labor voters would be also “shocked” to see the party refusing to preference a “local, progressive Greens woman in Prahran”, Angelica Di Camillo, who also ran at the byelection.

Labor is also running an open ticket in the neighbouring seat of Caulfield, held by the Liberals’ David Southwick on a 2.1% margin. But it is expected Southwick will see a swing in his favour and comfortably retain the seat.
after newsletter promotion

It is understood the local campaigns in Prahran and Caulfield requested the open ticket arrangement, which is consistent with the position Labor took at the 2025 federal election in the overlapping seat of Macnamara, held by Josh Burns, amid the height of the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza.
A Labor spokesperson said: “Our message is simple: put a 1 next to Labor candidates everywhere. We’re fighting for majority government.”
Caulfield is home to Victoria’s largest Jewish community, which also extends into St Kilda East in the Prahran electorate.

On Tuesday, the Liberals and Nationals also confirmed they would exchange preferences with One Nation, with the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, telling reporters how-to-vote cards for Coalition candidates would instruct voters to put Labor, the Greens and the Victorian Socialists “at the bottom of the ticket, and all other parties above that”.

Just hours after Wilson confirmed the position, One Nation moved to disendorse its Preston candidate, Franco Guardiani, over tweets, including one that described Hitler as the “GOAT”, an acronym which stands for greatest of all time.
The Victorian Liberal Senator Jane Hume told ABC’s Afternoon Briefing Guardiani’s tweets were “vile” and confirmed he would be last on the party’s how-to-vote material in the electorate.

articles.title: Pope Leo vs. Javier Milei: How political is the pope?
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV's tour of South America has drawn huge crowds — and a measure of political controversy. Perceived criticism of Argentina's leader, and earlier rebukes of Donald Trump, offer a glimpse…

image.caption: Pope Leo XIV and Argentine President Javier Milei met on SundayImage: Luis Robayo/AFP

blocks.text: The 2.5 million people lining the streets of Buenos Aires to get a glimpse of Pope Leo XIV on Monday left little doubt as to his influence in Argentina and beyond.

"It's very important for Argentinians, for our unity and, above all, to reaffirm faith in the Catholic Church in this country. Argentina is a country of faith, it's always been so," one attendee told DW of the open air Mass.

"The mood from the public about his visit is overwhelmingly positive," Justin McLellan, Vatican correspondent for the National Catholic Reporter, told DW from Argentina's capital. "I think that people are big fans of Leo."

The previous day, Leo had made a series of remarks which many observers took to be criticism of Argentine President Javier Milei and his strict austerity measures, sweeping cuts to social services and the elimination of thousands of public sector jobs.
Afterward, there were suggestions from some of the president's supporters online that the pope, who is returning to duty just a month after cancer surgery, had overstepped his role.
Pope urges Argentina's president to put people first

"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," said Leo, the first US-born pope, on Sunday. He also mentioned those who "despite hard work, nonetheless, struggle to meet their household's needs."
Leo doubled down on the message on a visit to a care home before Monday's Mass, where he preached to millions.
Pope Leo walks soft-power tightrope

"It's clearly targeting, without naming, the different policies that the president has put on recently," Jocelyne Cesari, a professor of religion and politics at the University of Birmingham in the UK, told DW, adding that Leo's words were "carefully calibrated."

Throughout its history, estimated by some at close to 2,000 years, the papacy has been a role with huge, and previously very direct, political power. Pope Innocent III, for example, was widely considered the most important man in the Europe in the late 11th and early 12th century. He wielded power over much of Europe and its monarchies, ensuring each territory was run according to Catholic doctrine.

blocks.caption: An estimated 2.5 million people lined the streets to see the pope in Buenos AiresImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: But in the modern day, that power has softened, with 20th and 21st century popes tending to intervene in a broader sense away from direct party politics and policy.

Leo's commitment to walking that tightrope was tested early in his papacy by US President Donald Trump, an ally of Milei, who called him "WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy" in a social media post in April.

"I do not look at my role as being political, a politician," responded Leo. "I'm not afraid of the Trump administration or speaking out loudly of the message of the Gospel, which is what I believe I am here to do, what the Church is here to do." It's a familiar stance, said Cesari.

"That's a line that all popes before him have walked. We tend to forget that the pope is the head of the state, is a diplomat and is a voice for more than 1 billion Catholics, so the role has always been political."
Can Pope Leo influence Argentina's election?
Both Cesari and McLellan agreed that Leo and his modern predecessors are keen to avoid party politics but instead offer guidance to the 1.4 billion Catholics in the world.

"The strategy of the pope is to position himself as a moral authority, his role is not just to say 'vote for X or Y.' His role is to say there are some moral teachings that can be applied to social life and communities, but people must make their personal decisions," said Cesari.

With Argentina a majority Catholic country, it stands to reason that the pope's word holds plenty of sway. But the longer-term question is whether Leo's perceived criticisms of Milei make a difference in Argentina's general election in October 2027.
Argentina loses 33 companies a day under Javier Milei

"People want to be drawn close to him [Leo]. I think the visit to Argentina could have an influence in the election in that he's certainly given his support to the Argentine bishops who have been critical of Milei's austerity policies and his cuts to social programs," said McLellan.
"I think that that could have an impact in the election and that it will elevate and raise the voice of the Catholic Church in Argentina."
Milei's battle with Catholic Church

But Cesari is not so sure that being sympathetic to a speech transfers to action at the ballot box. "They may revere and respect the pope. But is not clear that that what he says has a direct impact on individual voters," she said.

"His voice will be heard. But from the studies we have, there is not a clear, direct impact on elections. We know that Catholics do not vote in a bloc and we know that lots of them voted for Milei in 2023, even after he called [Leo's predecessor Pope] Francis the representative of evil on Earth."

Milei, a right-wing libertarian and outspoken critic of the ruling class, has long clashed with the Catholic Church. He also called Pope Francis, a native of Argentina, an "imbecile" in 2020 and accused him of promoting communism. He did, however, find a more conciliatory tone on Monday when he called the late Francis an "exceptional figure" and the "most important Argentine in history."

Leo is, McLellan added, "diplomatic by nature." With Trump and Milei both having taken swipes at the Catholic Church in a time of ongoing geopolitical turmoil, that looks to be a critical papal quality.

articles.title: Poa: Is there something wrong with going to China?
articles.summary: Poa asked what was wrong with going to China after another one of the defense team's witnesses at Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial was grilled about making a trip there.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 9:35pm

Attorney Michael Poa asked what was wrong with going to China after another one of the defense team's witnesses at Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial was grilled about making a trip there.

On Tuesday, Davao City Accountant Vingelin Bajan was asked about a visit to China she had made. This follows Monday's witness, Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, who was grilled about trips to China last year and earlier this year.

“I guess the question is, may masama ba sa pagpunta ng China? [Is there something wrong about going to China?] I think that's the question, but I don't want to give the answer, because again that's up to the senator-judges to determine and it's up to their appreciation kung may problema ba na pumunta ng China itong mga witnesses [whether there's a problem with these witnesses going to China],” Poa said in a press briefing following the trial session on Tuesday.

Poa said that it was ultimately up to the witnesses to answer questions about their trip and where the funds for these trips came from, whether it was their own personal money or if it was a trip sponsored by the Chinese government.
The defense would want their witnesses to answer questions straight, Poa said.

During Monday’s trial session, senator-judges had questioned Adalin for his trip to China, many details of which he said he did not remember. While he initially said he could not remember any trip to China, he later confirmed that he had made a trip together with other city department heads.
Adalin had also been grilled by senator-judges for his apparent inability to recall specific details about the trip, including where he traveled to specifically.
Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo has already defended Adalin, saying that his trips to China had nothing to do with his credibility as a witness.
“Ano namang kinalaman ng credibility ng isang government official kung meron siyang official trip to China? Para sa akin, wala,” Panelo said.
(What does a government official’s credibility have to do with an official trip to China? In my view, nothing.)— BM, GMA News
